profile.name: Benjamin Jordan
profile.summary: Hands-on technical leader with 20+ years of shipping people-first products. Currently working on LLM-native workflows for builders at [vetra.io](https://vetra.io) (MCP, RAG, structured agent FSMs), and AI-first products that solve problems for my local community.

skills.label: LLM-native products
skills.value: MCP, RAG, HITL, semantic APIs, structured loops, agent design

skills.label: Full-stack
skills.value: Go, TypeScript, C#, Java, Python, Obj-C, Unity, WebGL, CG

skills.label: Distributed systems & infrastructure
skills.value: CQRS, local-first CRDT/OT, Docker, K8s, AWS, GCP

skills.label: Leadership
skills.value: 0-to-1 product engineering, org building and hiring, xDev and vendor management

highlights: Invited maintainer of [Quicktype](https://github.com/quicktype/quicktype/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3Athegoldenmule+is%3Aclosed), serial contributor to [Nakama](https://github.com/heroiclabs/nakama), contributor to [Polygon Edge](https://github.com/0xPolygon/polygon-edge/pull/414) and [Antlr](https://github.com/antlr/antlr4/pull/2267).
[100+ published essays](#writing), with AI and agentic tooling the current focus.

events.title: Miscellaneous Writing
events.description: By no means an exhaustive list of my writing -- but some of the Greatest Hits.

children.title: My Workflow is Better than Yours — Week 2
children.subtitle: A cycle worth sharing. Again.
children.description: One week into using Hotseat as a primary interface for wrangling LLM coding agents. A native macOS Kanban app that queues plans, code, and commits — with worktrees, live tails, transition hooks, and a semantic CLI so LLMs can drive themselves.

children.title: The Value of Resistance
children.subtitle: On formation through friction.
children.description: Why difficulty, toil, and struggle are intrinsically valuable, and what we risk losing when programming no longer requires them.

children.title: The TikTok-ification of Programming
children.subtitle: Building software in 20-second bursts and losing something slower.
children.description: A reflection on how LLM-powered coding has compressed programming into short bursts of productivity.

children.title: File Over App Is an Old Idea
children.subtitle: A toast to an abstraction that has scaled for 50 years.
children.description: How Obsidian's 'file over app' philosophy traces back to the Unix pipe, the Thompson shell, and the 50-year-old idea that everything is a file.

children.title: The Myth of a Post-Programming World
children.subtitle: When you don't know history, don't guess about the future.
children.description: Why programming languages will always be needed.

children.title: The Shape of Software is Collapsing
children.subtitle: When 'build it' always beats 'buy it'.
children.description: AI coding tools are making custom software trivial to build, collapsing the layers of SaaS products that once seemed indispensable. What happens to the industry when the standard models disappear overnight?

children.title: How an LLM is making my bulletproof casual game
children.subtitle: Making your tools work together.

children.title: Low-Hanging LLM Fruit

children.title: The Collab Machine

children.title: The Read-Only Ouroboros

children.description: Programming is becoming in increasingly read-only. What are we at risk of losing?

children.title: What information is good for the world?

children.title: Hangman LiveOps
